notes: decimals() always returns 6; 32-byte transfer memos; TIP-403 policy registry; T6 receive policies redirect blocked transfers to ReceivePolicyGuard. Overview at https://tempo.xyz/developers/docs/protocol/tip20.

title: The "Payment" HTTP Authentication Scheme (draft-httpauth-payment-01, repository text of 2026-11-11)
publisher: Tempo Labs and Stripe (B. Ryan, J. Moxey, T. Meagher, J. Weinstein, S. Kaliski)
notes: Read in research/vendor/mpp-specs with git show origin/main at merge commit 7bb99c8542252b7aa4230c184e48f16c0ea1427a (PR #404, merged 2026-11-11T18:24:35Z). Edited in place under the -01 name, with no revision bump and no Datatracker submission. The rewritten section on other authentication schemes calls a Bearer token, HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421) or an attestation in an application-defined header field 'other authentication', which the Payment scheme does not define, register or constrain. Servers SHOULD verify it first and answer 401 (or the mechanism's own error) or 403 before any 402; when a request carries a Payment credential, servers MUST verify the other authentication before verifying, consuming or settling the credential, and on a denial on that basis MUST NOT settle, consume the challenge or credential, or issue a Payment-Receipt. The header parameter moves from MAY to SHOULD when the other authentication uses Authorization. Clients MUST resend their other authentication on the paid retry and MAY resend the same credential after a 401, or after a 403 whose Problem Details say other authentication denied access and nothing settled. Other mechanisms MAY bind their proofs to the challenge id; the draft defines no such binding. 403 now has two meanings, and servers SHOULD say which in the Problem Details body. A new security section scopes other authentication credentials to their origin and forbids sending them on a cross-origin redirect. The status codes table and the fields in the site's field tables are otherwise unchanged since 50309c8, apart from example fixes of 2026-10-26. At the same commit specs/intents still holds only the charge and subscription intents and specs/methods the same 11 method folders, and a git grep of specs/ finds none of the SDK header names Identity-Attestation, Identity-Attestation-Required, Identity-Presentation or Identity-Required.
